applications.title: Design Review Application
applications.source: City of Laguna Beach Design Review Application, "Updated August 2026" (the City's own file name dates it 08/05/2026), the section headed APPLICATION SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS, items 1 through 5. Retrieved 2026-08-14.
applications.when_to_file: The City states the trigger on page 1: "This application includes a comprehensive list of information and documents that are required to submit an application for a project requiring Design Review. Projects requiring Design Review are identified in the Laguna Beach Municipal Code. (See LBMC Section 25.05.040.)" The City also states: "Additional applications are required when an applicant is requesting additional entitlements, such as a Coastal Development Permit."

items.title: Design Review Application
items.detail: the completed City application form: project location (address and APN), applicant, applicant representative, and property owner contact information, and a project description that briefly describes the proposed improvements. The City files it through the Public Permit Portal and states "Applications without the required application fees will not be accepted."

items.title: Advance Deposit and Reimbursement Agreement and Title Report
items.detail: At intake, require the agreement and a current title report only when the City will peer-review a geotechnical or coastal-hazards report.

sections.heading: OTHER SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS FOR DESIGN REVIEW

items.title: Colored Elevations
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: "Required for building additions, new development, and when Design Review is triggered for exterior modifications to more than 50% of any street-facing façade of a building in a residential zone." Include all sides of structures and retaining walls over 5 feet in height. Include the maximum allowed building envelope. The City states not to show landscaping on the elevations.

items.title: Color and Material Selections
items.detail: include specifications and pictures of all exterior building finishes and roofing. Identify all proposed exterior colors, including manufacturer code specifications.

items.title: Paint swatches installed at the site
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: the Planning Commission is the design review authority [LBMC 25.05.040(F)(1)(b)]. At least one week before the scheduled public hearing, install two-foot-square minimum paint swatches at the project site for review under natural light.

items.title: 3D Color Renderings
items.detail: trigger confirmed by staff: new development or a major remodel under the Local Coastal Program's 50-percent major-remodel test. Renderings include landscaping, depictions of people to help evaluate scale, and accurate color. Provide front, rear, and side elevations. The City states a streetscape view showing surrounding development is optional but highly encouraged.

items.title: Digital Site Photos
items.detail: label file names with the direction of the photo and a description.
must_show: The direction of the photo
A description

items.title: Title Report
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: "Required for projects that require a topographic survey." Dated within one year of the application date. Title insurance or a title policy is a substitute, not the deliverable. Apply filing-context before requesting a replacement.

items.title: Affidavit and Use and Disclosure of Architectural Drawings
items.detail: the City states: "Affidavit and Use Architectural Drawings – sign and submit Exhibits I and J."

sections.heading: SUBMITTAL ITEMS DUE BEFORE THE CITY WILL NOTICE A PUBLIC HEARING

items.title: Noticing
items.detail: at least 30 calendar days before the public hearing, provide proof that the property has been posted with notice, and a receipt of payment to an approved Listing Service that prepares the mailing list of property owners within 300 feet and tenants within 100 feet. The Listing Service prints and mails the notices and provides staff an affidavit of mailing.

items.title: Early Neighbor Communication
items.detail: the City states early neighbor communication "for all Design Review projects shall occur prior to the project being scheduled for public hearing" [LBMC 25.05.040(C)(1)]. The applicant notifies property owners within 300 feet through a professional listing service, which certifies the accuracy and completeness of the list and the mailing date and provides a copy of the materials sent. The notice states applicant contact information, the project location, a description of the proposed project, and how to participate in the Design Review process. Exhibit K is the City's best-practices handout and Exhibit L is its outreach report template.

items.title: Historic Assessment
items.detail: Clearly identify the character-defining features and the development that will be removed and retained.

items.title: Water Quality Management Plan (WQMP) and WQMP Submittal Form (Exhibit M)
items.detail: An intake requirement only for a new home or major remodel on a slope greater than 25 percent, established from the survey or site facts. A slope alone does not establish new-home or major-remodel scope. At 25 percent or below, use the LID checklist. When the intake trigger applies, provide the WQMP and applicable submittal form; the same requirement governs its full-sized plan sheet.

items.title: Low Impact Development Checklist
items.detail: trigger: the developed slope is 25 percent or below. Do not demand a LID checklist as a substitute when WQMP is only a later staff determination for another scope over 25 percent.

items.title: Coastal Hazards Study and Bluff Edge Determination
items.detail: trigger as this application states it: "Required for oceanfront or bluff properties." The wave uprush and impact report considers a seasonally eroded beach combined with long-term (75 year) erosion, high tide conditions combined with long-term (75 year) projections for sea level rise, and storm waves from a 100-year event or a storm comparable to the 1982/83 El Niño event, prepared by a licensed civil engineer with expertise in coastal processes.

items.title: Geological, soils, or geotechnical study
items.detail: trigger: vacant and oceanfront sites. This application folds the bluff-edge content into this item: coastal bluff lots identify the bluff edge location (Land Use Element Definitions 101 and 102), any geologic hazards, any necessary mitigation measures, and statements that the site is suitable and the development will be safe from geologic hazard for its economic life. For development on oceanfront bluffs the report includes slope stability analyses and estimates of the long-term average bluff retreat or erosion rate over the expected life of the development. A licensed professional Engineering Geologist or Geotechnical Engineer prepares and signs it.

items.title: Hydraulic Report
items.detail: A parcel-level floodplain overlap alone does not trigger it. The later report is a professional engineer’s No-Rise / No-Impact certification supported by hydrologic and hydraulic analyses under LBMC Chapter 25.38.

items.title: Traffic Study
items.detail: trigger: subdivisions, new commercial developments, and major commercial renovations. The City states a traffic study may also be required to comply with the California Environmental Quality Act.

items.title: Parking Study
items.detail: trigger: the proposed project does not meet the minimum parking requirements, or LBMC Chapter 25.52 specifies one. This application states a parking study "may be required"; the Variance application states "will be required" for the same condition.

applications.title: ADU & JADU Application
applications.source: City of Laguna Beach ADU & JADU Application, "Updated August 2026" (the City's own file names date the August revision 08/05/2026), the section headed APPLICATION SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS, items 1 through 9..
applications.when_to_file: The City states the trigger on page 1: "This application includes a comprehensive list of information and documents that are required to submit an application for an accessory dwelling unit ('ADU') and/or junior accessory dwelling unit ('JADU')." The City also states: "Additional applications are required when an applicant is requesting additional entitlements, such as a Coastal Development Permit or a permit for Design Review," and gives its own examples of Design Review triggers on an ADU project: "design review is required for grading in exceed of 20 cubic yards outside of the building footprint, new vehicular access, retaining walls in excess of 5 feet, decks more than 3 feet above adjacent existing legal grade, and certain fences. (see LBMC Section 25.05.040.)" The City's development standards are at LBMC Chapter 25.17; the application notes that as of March 2025 Chapter 25.17 is replaced by Urgency Ordinance No. 1713.

items.title: ADU & JADU Application
items.detail: the completed City application form. The City files it through the Public Permit Portal and states "Applications without the required application fees will not be accepted."

items.title: Advance Deposit and Reimbursement Agreement and Title Report
items.detail: At intake, require the agreement and a current title report only when the City will peer-review a geotechnical or coastal-hazards report.

items.title: Coastal Development Permit Application
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: a CDP is required by LBMC Chapters 25.17 and 25.07, as further explained in Exhibit B of this application. The City states: "If required, the Coastal Development Permit Application must be processed concurrently with this ADU/JADU Application." The City also quotes Government Code Section 66329: the local government approves or denies the CDP within 60 days of a completed application, and processes it concurrently with the ADU application; section 66329(a) does not require a public hearing on it. After C1 establishes that the City/local government is the CDP decision maker and the CDP covers only the ADU, Government Code section 66329(c) also makes that local-government decision not subject to appeal under Public Resources Code section 30603, even if the parcel is ordinarily in a Chapter 25.07 appeal category. A CDP that also covers other development follows the appeal area. Do not apply this local procedure to a Coastal Commission decision or unresolved authority. For a conversion, as-built floor plans control the trigger: existing habitable space needs only the ADU & JADU Application; non-habitable space or new floor area also needs the CDP Application.

items.title: Construction Plans and Drawings
items.detail: the City states: "When preparing construction plans, the drawings need to clearly communicate design, structural integrity, and code compliance." The City's own footnote states the consequence: "The City will continue to process your application without the construction plans and drawings, but the application will not be deemed complete under the law without the construction plans and drawings."

items.title: Rent Reporting
items.detail: the form carries a write-in line: "Estimate of the projected annualized rent that will be charged for the ADU or JADU if the applicant intends to rent the unit." The City treats this line as voluntary: it never gates intake.

items.title: Percolation Test
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: "If the ADU or JADU will connect to an onsite wastewater - treatment system, the owner must include with the application a percolation test completed within the last five years or, if the percolation test has been recertified, within the last 10 years."

applications.title: Zone Clearance Application
applications.source: City of Laguna Beach Zone Clearance Application, "Updated July 2026", Section V (Application Submittal Requirements) and the exhibits that section cites. Retrieved 2026-08-14. Governing section: LBMC 25.05.045 (Zone Clearance).
applications.when_to_file: The City states the trigger on page 1 of the application: this is the application "for projects that DO NOT require a discretionary planning entitlement, such as Design Review or a Coastal Development Permit." A planner screens the application against the checklist below. When the application is complete and no discretionary entitlement is required, the City issues a zoning clearance and the applicant may then submit for a Building Permit.

items.title: Zone Clearance Application
items.detail: the completed City application form: project location (address and APN), applicant, applicant representative, and property owner contact information, and a project description that briefly describes the proposed use and improvements. The City files it through the Public Permit Portal.

items.title: Advance Deposit and Reimbursement Agreement and Title Report
items.detail: At intake, require the agreement and a current title report only when the City will peer-review a geotechnical or coastal-hazards report.

items.title: Completed Objective Design Standards checklists
items.detail: trigger: the applicant elects Chapter 25.13 for a new single-family or two-family primary dwelling, including an SB 9 project. Include the completed Chapter 2 General Design Standards checklist and exactly one applicant-selected Chapter 3 Form Group checklist (A, B, C, or D), with the corresponding plan-sheet location for every applicable standard. Source: City document 26790 §§1.2–1.4 and Chapters 2–3.

must_show: For "Revision (Construction)" the City prints one merged cell spanning the plan-sheet columns reading "All Plan Sheets Affected by Proposed Revision". Scope a revision packet to the sheets its own revision touches; do not apply another row's sheet set to it.
For "Tenant Improvement" the "if req." entry sits between the Elevation Views and Cross Sections columns in the extracted layout. The column it belongs to is ambiguous in the text extraction.

The matrix carries a "Staking Plan" column, but Section V contains no staking-plan item and Zone Clearance alone creates no staking requirement under LBMC 25.05.040(C)(2). Do not assign staking from an ADU or local ADU CDP label. If a separately reviewed component routes to B(1) or B(3), use that component's hearing rule (21 days for a first B(1) hearing; 14 days for ADR only after a Director/designee decision; 14 days for directed restaking).

items.title: Title Sheet
items.detail: provide address of site and assessor's parcel number, legal description of the site, and contact information for the property owner, project architect or designer, civil engineer, and other design professionals (names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses).
must_show: Include a detailed scope of work and a plan sheet index.
Include the Project Summary Table in the format and content of the City's template (Exhibit D).
State the zoning designation.
State site constraints, environmentally sensitive areas, and fire safety designation, if applicable. The City points to its GIS map for this information.

items.title: Topographic Survey
items.detail: trigger: Exhibit C requires a survey for the project's type. Required scale 1/8" = 1'-0". Depict existing conditions and all public and private easements. Prepared, signed, and stamped by a licensed surveyor or civil engineer. The Site Survey Requirements handout (Exhibit E) carries additional requirements.

items.title: Record of Survey
items.detail: Show all property boundary lines, public and private easements, and whether new monuments were set to show the boundary lines. Prepared, signed, and stamped by a licensed surveyor or civil engineer, and filed for processing with the County Surveyor's Office for review and recordation.

items.title: Site Plan
items.detail: trigger: Exhibit C requires a site plan for the project's type. Required scale 1/8" = 1'-0".
must_show: Include a north arrow (magnetic and project north).
Include a legend (line types, hatched and shaded areas, abbreviations).

Show and label all buildings on the lot. Delineate and dimension all lot boundaries, required setbacks, and existing and proposed structures at the narrowest point. Dimension the interior of garages and carports, exterior parking spaces, vehicular maneuvering, and back-up areas.
Show topographic contours at two-foot intervals covering the full site to the center of the right-of-way.

Label, locate, and dimension all proposed site hardscape improvements. Identify the height and material of all existing and proposed fences or walls, and show the location of any required pool security fencing.
Show average lot width and depth [LBMC 25.08.022].

Provide flagged height elevations at: the fixed datum point from a survey showing a permanent, identifiable benchmark in the field; the top of curb or centerline of the street right-of-way, midway between the projected side lot lines [LBMC 25.08.016]; the centerline of the street opposite the driveway and at the intersection of the driveway and front property line [LBMC 25.52.008(I)(3)(b)]; and both front and rear property corners [LBMC 25.08.034].

Label, dimension, and show the centerline of the right-of-way of record and the paved (improved) centerline width of all abutting streets and alleyways. Show all existing and proposed improvements within the right-of-way, including driveways, sidewalks, meters, and utility boxes and poles.
Depict the location and dimensions of all existing and proposed public or private easements and all property to be dedicated to the City for street or other purposes.
Note the average driveway gradient, calculated from the property line to the face of the garage or parking spaces [LBMC 25.52.008(I)(3)].
On vacant and oceanfront sites, show the immediate outline of existing structures on adjacent contiguous properties.
Locate and dimension the trash storage area [LBMC 25.53.012].

For new development, major remodels (defined in Exhibit F), and additions exceeding 50 percent of the existing structure size, note that all utility lines to the nearest existing pole will be undergrounded [LBMC 25.53.010]. Specify the type and location of the utility connection (pole or box) and indicate the size of all utility boxes.
Show the proposed connection to the public sewer system, if applicable.

items.title: Roof Plan
items.detail: trigger: Exhibit C requires a roof plan for the project's type. Required scale 1/8" = 1'-0". Dimension and show the existing and proposed roof plans.
must_show: On the existing roof plan, delineate and dimension the existing roof area and the proposed demolition areas (eaves are included in roof area). Provide a table that tallies the existing and demolition roof areas.

Show the roof form (ridges, hips, valleys, crickets, parapets) and note elevation heights of ridges, eaves, skylights, and chimneys. Show roof slopes and pitch, show the solar-ready roof area, and dimension eave overhangs.

items.title: Floor Plans (as-built and proposed)
items.detail: trigger: Exhibit C requires floor plans for the project's type. Required scale 1/4" = 1'-0".
must_show: Orient the plans to match the site plan, including a north arrow (magnetic and project north) and property lines.
Indicate the use and dimensions of all existing and proposed rooms and interior garages.

On the as-built floor plan, dimension and show the existing walls and the walls proposed to be demolished, rebuilt, and new. Provide a table that tallies the existing and demolished wall lengths in linear feet. Provide a legend identifying existing walls to remain (plain), existing walls to be rebuilt (shaded), walls to be demolished (dashed), and proposed new walls (dark shade).
Note the finish floor elevation of each level, including finish surface elevations for all decks, patios, terraces, and landings.

items.title: Elevation Views (as-built and proposed)
items.detail: trigger: Exhibit C requires elevation views for the project's type. Required scale 1/4" = 1'-0".
must_show: Label height elevations of roofs, floors, plate lines, decks, and railings. Dimension ceiling heights.
Differentiate new from existing construction using shading or crosshatching, and provide a legend stating what the shading or crosshatch represents.
Show existing grades as a dashed line and proposed grades as a solid line.
Illustrate the maximum allowed building envelope with dashed lines [LBMC 25.50.004(d)].
Include landscape site walls exceeding five feet in height.
On the as-built elevations, show and dimension the demolition areas using shading or crosshatch, and provide a legend stating what the shading or crosshatch represents.

items.title: Cross Sections
items.detail: trigger: Exhibit C requires cross sections for the project's type. Required scale 1/4" = 1'-0". Provide a minimum of two perpendicular views through the complete site showing the structure and the lines of existing and proposed grade. Include the maximum allowed building envelope and elevation heights, and site improvements such as walls, terraces, and pools or spas. The City states that existing and proposed building heights are measured from the outside structural walls, including retaining walls when below grade.

items.title: Floor Area Calculations
items.detail: trigger: Exhibit C requires floor area calculations for the project's type. Required scale 1/4" = 1'-0". Provide a separate, dimensioned plan using geometric shapes to show the method used to determine the existing and proposed floor areas. Identify living, garage, deck, and storage or mechanical areas, referenced to a table that itemizes and tallies each area. Floor area is calculated from the outside structural wall, including retaining walls when below grade.

items.title: Open Space Calculations
items.detail: the matrix marks no open space calculations for any of the ministerial project types. Required scale 1/4" = 1'-0". Trigger stated by the City: "For projects that are subject to the open space requirements of LBMC 25.50.010, provide a separate dimensioned plan showing open space areas and calculations. Refer to the development standards of the underlying zoning district in Title 25 to determine applicability."

items.title: Grading and Drainage Plan
items.detail: trigger confirmed by staff: the project proposes grading and its cut and/or fill outside the existing building footprint exceeds 20 cubic yards; grading inside that footprint does not count. The matrix heads its column "Grading & Drainage (When > 20 Cu. Yd.)", marks it for the Grading and Hardscape project types, and marks it "if req." for an accessory dwelling unit, an addition under 10 percent, and retaining walls.
must_show: Provide a preliminary grading and drainage plan with the proposed cut and fill area delineated. Provide slope profiles to illustrate the extent of the proposed grading. Show contours for existing conditions and proposed work.

For project sites containing a mapped significant watercourse or sensitive habitat, show temporary protective barriers beyond the required setback for the protection of the watercourse and sensitive habitat during construction.

items.title: Landscape Plan
items.detail: the matrix marks a landscape plan for the Landscape Improvements project type only. Required scale 1/8" = 1'-0". When landscape scope is in play, provide landscape plans including new and existing-to-remain plant material. The Landscape Submittal Checklist (Exhibit G) carries the comprehensive list of requirements. A pool, ground-level lounge deck, patio cover, or lawn shown incidentally does not by itself create landscape scope.
must_show: For R-1 zoned property, provide a landscape open space dimensioned plan [LBMC 25.10.008(O)].

items.title: Lighting Plan
items.detail: trigger: Exhibit C requires a lighting plan for the project's type. The matrix marks no lighting plan for any of the ministerial project types, so on a Zone Clearance this sheet is rarely in play. Required scale 1/8" = 1'-0". Show exterior site lighting, including all lighting fixtures proposed for the exterior of the building (soffit and surface mounted). Include a summary table, keyed to the plan, indicating proposed fixture type, quantity, lumens, and wattage. Include lighting cut sheets for verification against the City's Good Neighbor Outdoor Lighting requirements [LBMC 7.70].

items.title: Fire Department Site Access Plan
items.detail: Required only when proposed new building-type construction (a new home, detached ADU, or other detached structure) could block existing fire access. Attached ADUs, additions, grading alone, interior work, roof or deck work, and surface replacement never trigger it. Neither VHFHSZ nor another hazard overlay triggers it. A legible, project-identifiable site-access depiction satisfies intake. Completed Fire review and technical adequacy belong to Building/Fire.

items.title: Fire Protection Plan
items.detail: the current City application package or an identity-qualified official City designation combined with the form's exact VHFHSZ trigger may establish that this sheet applies. Planning checks presence, legibility, and identity only and routes it to Fire/Building.

items.title: Fuel modification program
items.detail: an identity-qualified official FM designation combined with the current form's exact trigger may establish applicability. Planning checks presence, legibility, and identity only. Fire/Building decides technical content and any Alternative Materials and Methods request; raw overlay truthiness is not the Planning decision rule.

items.title: Site and Right-of-Way Improvement Plan
items.detail: Required scale 1/8" = 1'-0". When applicable, provide a topographic survey (including public and private easements) and the improvement overlay.

sections.heading: ADDITIONAL REQUIRED INFORMATION FOR CERTAIN SITES

items.title: Arch Beach Heights neighboring-window exhibit
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: the parcel is in the Arch Beach Heights Specific Plan area and the project proposes new windows. Dash in the horizontally projected outline of windows on existing neighboring structures within 10 feet of the proposed new windows on the elevation views [LBMC 25.35.090(B)(3)].

items.title: Diamond Crestview Construction Staging Plan and Constraint Analysis
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: the Diamond Crestview Specific Plan applies. Refer to p. IV-10 of the Specific Plan.

items.title: Affidavit
items.detail: the City states: "Affidavit – sign and submit Exhibits H." The property owner signs it. The City states acceptable signatures are a wet signature (a scan is acceptable) or an authenticated electronic signature such as DocuSign, and that a typed name alone is not sufficient.

A slope alone does not establish new-home or major-remodel scope. At 25 percent or below, use the LID checklist. When the intake trigger applies, provide the WQMP and applicable submittal form; the same requirement governs its full-sized plan sheet.

items.detail: trigger: the developed slope is 25 percent or below. Do not demand a LID checklist as a substitute when WQMP is only a later staff determination for another scope over 25 percent.

items.title: Coastal Hazards Study and Bluff Edge Determination
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: oceanfront or bluff property, when the project proposes new development (including accessory structures), major remodels, or additions. The wave uprush and impact report considers a seasonally eroded beach combined with long-term (75 year) erosion, high tide conditions combined with long-term (75 year) projections for sea level rise, and storm waves from a 100-year event or a storm comparable to the 1982/83 El Niño event. A licensed civil engineer with expertise in coastal processes prepares it. Coastal bluff lots identify the bluff edge location per Land Use Element Definitions 101 and 102; Exhibit J carries the City's guidance.

items.title: Geological, soils, or geotechnical study
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: vacant and oceanfront sites. A licensed professional Engineering Geologist or Geotechnical Engineer prepares and signs it.

items.title: Hydraulic Report
items.detail: A parcel-level floodplain overlap alone does not trigger it. The later report is a professional engineer’s No-Rise / No-Impact certification supported by hydrologic and hydraulic analyses under LBMC Chapter 25.38.

items.title: Traffic Study
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: subdivisions, new commercial developments, and major commercial renovations. The study identifies measures to mitigate identified impacts. The City states a traffic study may also be required to comply with the California Environmental Quality Act.

items.title: Parking Study
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: the proposed project does not meet the minimum parking requirements, or LBMC Chapter 25.52 specifies one.

applications.title: Conditional Use Permit Application
applications.source: City of Laguna Beach Conditional Use Permit Application, "Updated July 2026", the section headed APPLICATION SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS, items 1 through 11. Retrieved 2026-08-14. The City republished the form on 2026-09-17 as "Updated August 2026" (https://www.lagunabeachcity.net/home/showpublisheddocument/26463/639252307038230000). Items 1 through 11 are unchanged in that edition.
applications.when_to_file: The City states the trigger on page 1: "Some uses are allowed in a zoning district but may not fit every location because of their size, intensity, or other characteristics. These uses require a CUP because they could have moderate to significant impacts on the site or nearby properties." The form covers "an application for a Conditional Use Permit ('CUP'), including a CUP amendment." The City states the Planning Commission reviews all CUP applications, and that where a project requires multiple entitlements the Planning Commission is the approval authority except as the Municipal Code otherwise specifies. The City also states: "Additional applications are required when an applicant is requesting additional entitlements, such as a permit for Design Review and/or a Coastal Development Permit."

items.title: Conditional Use Permit Application
items.detail: the completed City application form: project location (address and APN), applicant, applicant representative, and property owner contact information, and a project description. For business uses the City asks the description to include a brief description of the business operations. The City files it through the Public Permit Portal and states "Applications without the required application fees will not be accepted."

items.title: Advance Deposit and Reimbursement Agreement and Title Report
items.detail: At intake, require the agreement and a current title report only when the City will peer-review a geotechnical or coastal-hazards report.

items.title: Letter of Intent and Justification
items.detail: the City states: "A written letter with the information required below is required to be submitted by the owner or agent/applicant with the application." This is one deliverable. The content bullets below are what a reviewer inspects inside it; they are not separate completeness rows.
must_show: Operational information: a complete description of the intended uses, including hours of operation; the number of employees anticipated during peak hours; a sample beverage menu and the associated California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control license type if alcoholic beverages are proposed to be served or sold; and a list of products for retail sale, a food and beverage menu, or a list of services.

For food services: a delivery plan (loading and unloading area, truck size and route, delivery hours, and methods to minimize traffic impacts); a trash collection plan (size, quantity, location and type of bins, truck routes, collection frequency, spill control, means of trash transport to the bins, and methods to minimize traffic impacts); a kitchen equipment schedule including any existing or proposed grease interceptor devices; a mechanical equipment and vent schedule for new or replacement exterior equipment with keynotes tying the schedule to symbols on a roof or site plan; and the occupant load based on Building Code requirements.

A description of any live entertainment offered on the premises and whether prerecorded music would be provided, including proposed speaker placement, the type of live entertainment, the performance area, and performance hours.
Occupancy information, such as class sizes and maximum restaurant seating count.
A list of other similar businesses operated by the applicant or franchise.

Written justification addressing the findings. The City prints one set of findings and questions for sites outside the Downtown Specific Plan [LBMC 25.05.030] and a different set for sites inside it. Inside the Downtown Specific Plan the City also requires a written justification for each applicable special finding: full-service restaurants; non-full-service restaurants and food services; art galleries; formula-based businesses and souvenir stores; exceptions to the single-story height limit; and seasonal uses coinciding with the art festivals (see pages 160–161 of the Downtown Specific Plan).

sections.heading: BASIC SITE AND FLOOR PLANS (EXHIBIT B)

items.title: Basic Site Plan (Exhibit B)
items.detail: "You may draw the basic site plan or use the City's Geographic Information System (GIS) or other mapping system to create the plan. Instructions for preparing a site plan through the City's GIS map viewer are available here. The plan must include all of the following:"

items.title: Tenant Mix Table
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: commercial projects on multi-tenant sites. Provide a table listing, for each tenant, the business name, type of business, size of tenant space in square feet, and for restaurants the seat count. For vacant tenant spaces, provide this information for the most recent occupant.

items.title: Digital Photographs
items.detail: interior and exterior project site photos. Label file names with the direction of the photo and a description. The City states internet photos such as Google Maps are not acceptable because they may not show current conditions.
must_show: The direction of the photo
A description

items.title: Title Report
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: "Required for projects that require a topographic survey." Dated within one year of the application date. Title insurance or a title policy is a substitute, not the deliverable. Apply filing-context before requesting a replacement.

items.title: Owner Affidavit and Use and Disclosure of Architectural Drawings
items.detail: the City states: "sign and submit Exhibits I and J." Exhibit I is titled "Affidavit"; Exhibit J is titled "Use and Disclosure of Architectural Drawings."

items.title: Hazardous Waste & Substances Form (Exhibit K)
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: commercial, mixed-use, and multi-family projects. Complete and return the form at Exhibit K.

items.title: Parking and Traffic Studies
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: CUP applications "for shared parking, four or more in-lieu parking certificates, or innovative parking solutions as prescribed by Section 25.52.006 of the Laguna Beach Municipal Code." A qualified professional prepares the study. The City retains a third party at the applicant's cost to review it, and states an initial deposit of $5,000 is required.

sections.heading: SUBMITTAL ITEMS DUE BEFORE THE CITY WILL NOTICE A PUBLIC HEARING

items.title: Noticing
items.detail: at least 30 calendar days before the public hearing, provide proof that the property has been posted with notice, and a receipt of payment to an approved Listing Service that prepares the mailing list of property owners within 300 feet and tenants within 100 feet. The Listing Service prints and mails the notices and provides staff an affidavit of mailing. This is a pre-hearing item, not a completeness item.

applications.title: Variance Application
applications.source: City of Laguna Beach Variance Application, "Updated July 2026", the section headed APPLICATION SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS, items 1 through 5. Retrieved 2026-08-14.
applications.when_to_file: The City states the trigger on page 1: "This application includes a comprehensive list of information and documents that are required to submit an application for a variance." On when a variance applies, the City states that the variance procedure "is designed to permit adjustments to the zoning regulations when there are special or extraordinary circumstances applying to a parcel of land or building which prevent the property from being used to the extent intended by the zoning regulations," and that "A variance is intended to be the rare exception, not the rule." The City also states: "Additional applications are required when an applicant is requesting additional entitlements, such as a permit for Design Review." The procedures are at LBMC 25.05.025.

items.title: Variance Application
items.detail: the completed City application form: project location (address and APN), applicant, applicant representative, and property owner contact information, a project description, and the variance request itself — the City prints "I hereby request a Variance from the following provisions of the Zoning Code" as a write-in field. The City files it through the Public Permit Portal and states "Applications without the required application fees will not be accepted."

items.title: Written justification for the four findings
items.detail: the application form carries four write-in narrative answers, one per finding, under the heading "STATE JUSTIFICATION FOR REQUEST (ATTACH ADDITIONAL SHEETS IF NEEDED)." The City states the decision-making authority must make all four findings, each supported by substantial evidence: special circumstances applicable to the property; necessity for the preservation and enjoyment of a substantial property right; no detriment to public health, safety, convenience and welfare or injury to property improvements in the vicinity; and no conflict with the objectives of the zoning ordinance or the General Plan. Presence means the justification narratives are in the packet. Whether they are persuasive is the Planning Commission's call, never a completeness call.

items.title: Advance Deposit and Reimbursement Agreement and Title Report
items.detail: At intake, require the agreement and a current title report only when the City will peer-review a geotechnical or coastal-hazards report.

items.title: Digital Site Photos
items.detail: label file names with the direction of the photo and a description.
must_show: The direction of the photo
A description

items.title: Title Report
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: "Required for projects that require a topographic survey." Dated within one year of the application date. Title insurance or a title policy is a substitute, not the deliverable. Apply filing-context before requesting a replacement.

items.title: Affidavit and Use and Disclosure of Architectural Drawings
items.detail: the City states: "Affidavit and Use Architectural Drawings – sign and submit Exhibits H and I."

sections.heading: SUBMITTAL ITEMS DUE BEFORE THE CITY WILL NOTICE A PUBLIC HEARING

items.title: Noticing
items.detail: at least 30 calendar days before the public hearing, provide proof that the property has been posted with notice, and a receipt of payment to an approved Listing Service that prepares the mailing list of property owners within 300 feet and tenants within 100 feet. The Listing Service prints and mails the notices and provides staff an affidavit of mailing.

items.title: Historic Assessment
items.detail: Clearly identify the character-defining features and the development that will be removed and retained.

items.title: Water Quality Management Plan (WQMP) and WQMP Submittal Form (Exhibit J)
items.detail: An intake requirement only for a new home or major remodel on a slope greater than 25 percent, established from the survey or site facts. A slope alone does not establish new-home or major-remodel scope. At 25 percent or below, use the LID checklist. When the intake trigger applies, provide the WQMP and applicable submittal form; the same requirement governs its full-sized plan sheet.

items.title: Low Impact Development Checklist
items.detail: trigger: the developed slope is 25 percent or below. Do not demand a LID checklist as a substitute when WQMP is only a later staff determination for another scope over 25 percent.

items.title: Coastal Hazards Study and Bluff Edge Determination
items.detail: trigger stated by the City: oceanfront or bluff property, when the project proposes new development (including accessory structures), major remodels, or additions. The wave uprush and impact report considers a seasonally eroded beach combined with long-term (75 year) erosion, high tide conditions combined with long-term (75 year) projections for sea level rise, and storm waves from a 100-year event or a storm comparable to the 1982/83 El Niño event, prepared by a licensed civil engineer with expertise in coastal processes. Coastal bluff lots identify the bluff edge location per Land Use Element Definitions 101 and 102; Exhibit L carries the City's guidance.

items.title: Geological, soils, or geotechnical study
items.detail: trigger: vacant and oceanfront sites. A licensed professional Engineering Geologist or Geotechnical Engineer prepares and signs it.

items.title: Hydraulic Report
items.detail: A parcel-level floodplain overlap alone does not trigger it. The later report is a professional engineer’s No-Rise / No-Impact certification supported by hydrologic and hydraulic analyses under LBMC Chapter 25.38.

items.title: Traffic Study
items.detail: trigger: subdivisions, new commercial developments, and major commercial renovations. The City states a traffic study may also be required to comply with the California Environmental Quality Act.

items.title: Parking Study
items.detail: trigger: the proposed project does not meet the minimum parking requirements, or LBMC Chapter 25.52 specifies one. This application states a parking study "will be required"; the Design Review application states "may be required" for the same condition.

applications.title: Sign Permit Application
applications.source: City Sign Permit Application Package, Updated July 2026, APPLICATION SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS §§1–4 and Exhibit D, “What information is required?” Verified 2026-09-08.

items.title: Sign Permit Application
items.detail: cover and §4: completed application for the sign, with the signed owner affidavit and Use and Disclosure of Architectural Drawings (Exhibits A and B). A typed name alone is not an authenticated signature.

items.title: Sign Permit fee status
items.detail: §1: inspect available City fee status using the lane's fee policy.

items.title: Scaled sign drawings
items.detail: §2, first bullet: drawings of all proposed signs, with dimensions, area computation, location, height above ground, wording/graphics, letter size/font, materials, colors and lighting elements, if any. For a new or amended Master Sign Program include existing signs. Record evidence on the actual sign drawing, rather than substituting a building floor plan.

items.title: Sign site plan
items.detail: §2, second bullet: a scaled site plan locating the sign and building/suite and identifying its street frontage length. This source does not require a separately stamped topographic survey for every sign.

items.title: Building or suite elevation drawing for signage
items.detail: — §2, second bullet: a scaled elevation showing the building or suite and frontage. A freestanding sign elevation alone does not establish that the building/suite elevation exists.

items.title: Color photographs of elevations and existing signs
items.detail: — §2, third bullet: current site photographs covering those subjects. A proposed-sign rendering alone is not a photograph of existing conditions. If there are no existing signs, establish that fact rather than demanding photos of nonexistent signs.

items.title: Sign lighting specifications
items.detail: §2, fourth bullet: when illumination is proposed, provide lighting specifications identifying the fixtures or system.

items.title: Coordinated master sign standards
items.detail: §3, first bullet: common standards for lettering, sizes, style, colors, types, placement, lighting, quantity and materials when the program trigger is established.

items.title: Master sign program plot plan
items.detail: §3, second bullet: locations and sizes of existing/proposed signs relative to buildings, parking, driveways, streets and landscape. The sign site plan can supply both artifacts if its content does so; cite the same evidence without duplicate applicant requests.

items.title: Confirm additional Sign Guide materials
items.detail: The guide adds an 8½ × 11 inch material/color sample board, broader existing-sign drawings and electrical/wiring/fixture-brochure detail. It says lighting comes from above, whereas §2 also permits qualifying halo illumination.

applications.title: Revocable Encroachment Permit Application
applications.source: City of Laguna Beach Revocable Encroachment Permit Application, "Updated July 2026", the section headed APPLICATION SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS, items 1 through 6, plus the application form and Exhibits A, B and C. Retrieved 2026-08-14.
applications.when_to_file: The City states the trigger on page 1: a Revocable Encroachment Permit ("REP") "may allow minor construction in an otherwise unimproved, unused public right-of-way." The City limits the class of project to "minor structures such as low fences and retaining walls, walkways, stairs and construction incidentally related to landscape activities such as steppingstones, walking surfaces, planter areas and irrigation systems." The City also states a REP "shall not be used for any structure or improvement that, if demand is made for its removal, will create any nonconforming conditions or unlawful conditions under the provisions of the municipal code or any other codes, regulations or standards incorporated therein." The REP "consists of discretionary approval by the Community Development Director or their designee, following a noticed public hearing." The City states that use and maintenance of an encroachment in the public right-of-way "is not a right but a privilege extended by the City acting as the custodian of the overall public interest." The City directs the applicant to the procedures for a revocable encroachment permit at LBMC 11.50 and to the Zoning Code more generally at Title 25. The City also states: "Additional applications are required when an applicant is requesting additional entitlements, such as Design Review."

items.title: Revocable Encroachment Permit Application
items.detail: the completed City application form. The form carries the project location (address and APN), the applicant, applicant representative, and property owner contact information, and a description field. The City prints the description instruction as "Briefly describe the project in its entirety and more specifically the improvements proposed to be located in the right of way" — read the description for both halves. The City states all communications go to the emails in file. The City files the application through the Public Permit Portal and states "Applications without the required application fees will not be accepted."

items.title: Encroachment Plan
items.detail: item 2. The City states: "A detailed plan shall be on an 8 ½" x 11" sheet of paper entitled 'Encroachment Plan,' drawn clearly and legibly using conventional drafting practices." The City lists the contents: - The plan is based on accurate field measurements, at a scale of no less than 1" = 20', and shows existing gradients and improvements within twenty-five feet of the project area (item 2a). - Property lines, easements, drainage patterns and cultural features are shown true to scale and dimension within twenty-five feet of the project area. The plan identifies the complete right-of-way, and identifies the adjacent and opposite edge-of-pavement. If the property lies within 25 feet of a cul-de-sac, the plan identifies the complete cul-de-sac right-of-way and edge of pavement (item 2b). - Proposed improvements are shown legibly and accurately as to line and grade, including surface elevations, wall heights, fence heights, cut/fill slopes and materials (items 2c and 2d). - Grading information is shown if applicable (item 2e).

items.title: Geological, soils, or geotechnical study
items.detail: trigger stated by the City in item 2e: "If the proposal involves the grading of more than twenty cubic yards, a geotechnical report is also required."

items.title: Design Review Permit Application
items.detail: item 3. The City states: "Design Review Permit Application. Submit concurrent, if required." Do not decide from this file whether Design Review is required.

items.title: Affidavit
items.detail: Exhibit A. The property owner signs it and certifies the seven statements the City prints, including that the information in the application is true, that the owner has read and understands LBMC Chapter 25.05, and that the owner is the legal owner and consents to the filing. The City states acceptable signatures are a wet signature (a scan is acceptable) or an authenticated electronic signature such as DocuSign, and that a typed name alone is not sufficient.

Exhibit C. The applicant signs three separate statements: that the application's list of information and documents is the criteria the City applies to determine completeness under Government Code Sections 65940 and 65941; that the applicant understands the completeness review procedure under Sections 65940 and 65943; and a certification of compliance with Government Code Section 65962.5 on the lists of hazardous waste and substance facilities and sites. Apply the same signature rule as the affidavit.

sections.heading: SUBMITTAL ITEMS DUE BEFORE THE CITY WILL NOTICE A PUBLIC HEARING

items.title: Noticing
items.detail: item 4a. At least 20 calendar days before the public hearing, provide proof that the property has been posted with notice, and a receipt of payment to an approved Listing Service that prepares the mailing list of property owners within 300 feet and tenants within 100 feet of the subject property. The Listing Service prints and mails the public notices and provides staff an affidavit of mailing by the date staff specifies. This application states 20 calendar days. The Variance application states 30. Use 20 here; it is this application's number.

must_show: Site Posting — item 5a, due before the public hearing. Staff sends the applicant the public hearing notice. The applicant posts it on the property 10 days before the hearing. Staff also provides a Posting Affidavit form, which the applicant completes and returns before the hearing.

Notarized Revocable License and Encroachment Permit Agreement — item 6a and Exhibit B, due only if the REP is approved. The City states that once the 14-day appeal period has lapsed, the City returns the executed agreement to the applicant for recording with the Orange County Clerk. Exhibit B is the agreement form itself, signed by the Community Development Director and notarized, and accepted and notarized by the property owner.
a. It should be located in a manner that is not hazardous to the traveling public, including motorists, bicyclists and pedestrians.
b. It should be sufficiently set back from the edge of pavement or street centerline to provide adequate travel, parking and walking lanes.

c. It should not conflict with preexisting public utility structures, especially hydrants, vault and service meters, in any manner that necessitates relocation thereof at public expense or causes any other unacceptable interference, including impediments to the maintenance, relocation or repair of pipelines, conduits or substructures of any public utility.
d. It will not preclude public access, use or enjoyment of any area that has historically established such access, use or enjoyment.
e. It is not precedent setting in nature to the extent that it creates a noticeable projection into the streetscape as established by existing construction and improvements on neighboring properties.
f. It does not create structures of unusual or unacceptable appearance, form, shape or height that detract from the general quality of the streetscape.

applications.title: Wireless Facility Permit Application
applications.source: Wireless Facility Permit Application, Updated April 2026, §VIII REQUIREMENTS, printed pages 5–8 (A.1–A.18), and §I. Verified 2026-09-08. The source repeats A.1 for fees and A.2 for noticing; stable keys distinguish those separate rows.

items.title: Wireless Facility Permit Application
items.detail: — A.1 and A.18: completed application/checklist, with applicable sections answered (explained N/A allowed) and owner affidavit/drawing disclosure, Exhibits B and C. Record the exhibits' evidence within this application. §III requests representative authorization when representative and applicant differ, and an operator engineering/maintenance contact.

items.title: Wireless fee and deposit status
items.detail: Preserve the lane's fee timing rule.

items.title: Advance Deposit and Reimbursement Agreement
items.detail: At intake, require the agreement and a current title report only when the City will peer-review a geotechnical or coastal-hazards report.

items.title: Property owner's authorization
items.detail: A.2: when facility and property owners differ, an executed letter authorizing submission.

items.title: Facility description and purpose
items.detail: A.3: written description of the facility and why it is proposed. §V also asks for equipment scope and whether associated cabling is underground or aerial.

items.title: Detailed engineering plans and report
items.detail: A.4: engineered drawings/report addressing minimum technological height/diameter, visible component photos/model names, power output/frequency, antenna/equipment capacity and support-structure suitability. Recognize the artifact before assessing design adequacy.

items.title: Alternative-site and configuration justification
items.detail: — A.5: comparative study explaining alternatives considered and why they are not viable or are more intrusive. A generic project description is not this study.

items.title: Scaled facility architectural plans
items.detail: A.6: site, elevations and equipment details, including the visible-component finish note. Evaluate these as facility plans; do not rename pole/footing sections building floor plans.

items.title: Visual impact analysis
items.detail: A.7: existing/proposed photo simulations from three viewing angles with adequate surroundings. The source specifies equal-sized before/after images, two per page, one angle per page. A raw site photograph alone does not establish a simulation. Keep actual visual impacts for plan check.

items.title: RF categorical exclusion checklist
items.detail: A.8: record the checklist and its determination. Do not infer exclusion from a small antenna, solar power or a technological-height report.

items.title: RF exposure compliance report
items.detail: A.9: required unless A.8 establishes categorical exclusion. The source asks for projected RF modeling, an executive summary and exposure at ground level/nearby buildings within 30 feet. A height-justification report is not an exposure report.

items.title: FAA documentation
items.detail: A.10: document the FAA disposition. The table gives no additional explanation.

items.title: Noise study
items.detail: A.11: facilities with passive cooling (no fans) are exempt.

items.title: Traffic control plan
items.detail: A.12: the listed plan for work in the public right-of-way. A.1 permits explained N/A; inspect that evidence. Do not confuse the plan with the later construction work permit.

items.title: Landscape plan for facility screening
items.detail: A.13: only when landscaping mitigates the facility's visual impact. Include plant identity, mature and maintained dimensions, installation size, mature-size symbols, irrigation/control type and maintenance responsibility. For this application use A.13, not additional generic landscape demands.

items.title: Facility service area information
items.detail: A.14: locate the description/map of the facility's service area; do not infer it from the site address.

items.title: Right to access public right-of-way
items.detail: A.15: inspect the access-right evidence. It is distinct from the authorization to submit in A.2; identify a shared instrument only when its text establishes both. Apply public-owner uncertainty guidance where the required mechanism is unresolved.

items.title: Facility mock-up
items.detail: A.16: applies to a Planning Commission WFP on a new support structure, except a one-for-one replacement within five feet of the proposed project. A photograph or rendering does not prove a physical mock-up.

items.title: Other public agency application requirements
items.detail: — A.17: identify the applicable agencies/requirements, or an explained N/A under A.1. This identification is not proof that every later agency permit must already be issued.

items.title: Public noticing package
items.detail: A.2 noticing row: where the selected approval requires notice, the source describes the listing-service receipt and recipient list. Do not require applicant-generated mailing materials where the source says the listing service supplies them.

application_index.title: The application matching the project's entitlement path
application_index.detail: every project files at least one of the applications named below. The application, signed by the property owner, is a baseline deliverable. Signature rule, stated by the City on the application forms themselves: an acceptable signature is a wet signature (a scan is acceptable) or an authenticated electronic signature such as DocuSign; a typed name alone is not sufficient. Where a form carries more than one owner signature line, every line must be signed.

application_index.title: Zone Clearance Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: "for projects that DO NOT require a discretionary planning entitlement, such as Design Review or a Coastal Development Permit." Governing section: LBMC 25.05.045.

application_index.title: Design Review Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: "for a project requiring Design Review. Projects requiring Design Review are identified in the Laguna Beach Municipal Code. (See LBMC Section 25.05.040.)"

application_index.title: Coastal Development Permit Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: the Coastal Act and the City's certified Local Coastal Program require a CDP "for all development within the coastal zone, unless specifically exempted or excluded (see Laguna Beach Municipal Code Section 25.07.008 and 25.07.010, respectively)."

application_index.title: Variance Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: the variance procedure "is designed to permit adjustments to the zoning regulations when there are special or extraordinary circumstances applying to a parcel of land or building which prevent the property from being used to the extent intended by the zoning regulations." The City adds: "A variance is intended to be the rare exception, not the rule." Procedures: LBMC 25.05.025.

application_index.title: Conditional Use Permit Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: "Some uses are allowed in a zoning district but may not fit every location because of their size, intensity, or other characteristics. These uses require a CUP because they could have moderate to significant impacts on the site or nearby properties." Covers a CUP amendment as well. Regulations: LBMC 25.05.030.

application_index.title: ADU & JADU Application
application_index.detail: the City's Applications & Handouts page lists this form as the "ADU Application"; the form itself is headed "ADU & JADU Application". Trigger as the City states it: "an application for an accessory dwelling unit ('ADU') and/or junior accessory dwelling unit ('JADU')." Standards: LBMC Chapter 25.17, which the application notes is replaced by Urgency Ordinance No. 1713 as of March 2025.

application_index.title: SB 9 Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: an application "for a SB9 Lot Split or Two-Unit development (see Government Code Sections 65852.21 and 66411.7)". The City's form states: "A Coastal Development Permit is required for SB9 Lot Split or SB9 Two-Unit development. The SB9 application(s) will not be deemed complete until a copy of a legally approved and final Coastal Development Permit for the SB9 application(s) has been submitted." Both of the form's checklists repeat this: Lot Split item I ("Approved Coastal Development Permit") and Two-Unit section H ("Copy of legally approved and final coastal development permit"). A pending CDP application, or one filed at the same time, does not meet this requirement. The SB 9 application stays incomplete until the submittal includes a copy of the approved, final CDP.

trigger as the City states it: "This form serves as the preliminary application for housing development projects seeking vesting rights pursuant to SB 330, the Housing Crisis Act of 2019." The City states the applicant has 180 days after submitting it to file a full application. The City publishes no submittal checklist with this form: it is a preliminary application form with numbered information fields.

application_index.title: Lot Line Adjustment Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: "an application for Lot Line Adjustment ('LLA')." Regulated by LBMC 21.08.030.

application_index.title: Tentative Parcel and Tract Map Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: "an application to subdivide land requiring the approval of a Tentative Parcel Map or Tentative Tract Map," and the requirements for condominium conversions per LBMC Chapter 25.47. The City states a Tentative Parcel Map is required for a subdivision creating four or fewer parcels and a Tentative Tract Map for five or more. Filing is governed by LBMC 21.08.090.

application_index.title: Revocable Encroachment Permit Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: a REP "may allow minor construction in an otherwise unimproved, unused public right-of-way," limited to minor structures such as low fences and retaining walls, walkways, stairs, and construction incidental to landscape activities. The City states the REP is a discretionary approval by the Community Development Director following a noticed public hearing, and that the application itself requires a Design Review Permit Application.

application_index.title: Sign Permit Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: a Sign Permit is required when "constructing, moving, altering, establishing, painting or creating a temporary or permanent sign in any area of the City, including on windows"; when placing signs in interior areas positioned primarily to be read or visible from the exterior; and when placing luminous tube signs inside a building if visible through a window.

application_index.title: Reasonable Accommodation Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: a request "for consideration for reasonable accommodation in accordance with LBMC 25.05.080," meaning flexibility in the application of land use, zoning and building regulations, or waiver of certain requirements, when necessary to eliminate barriers to fair housing opportunities.

application_index.title: Floodplain Development Permit Application for Residential Development
application_index.detail: the City's form states no trigger sentence and cites no Municipal Code section; it names its scope only in its title and its "Development Proposed" check-box block. The form carries no tailored submittal checklist.

application_index.title: Historic Register Placement Application
application_index.detail: an owner-initiated letter to the Heritage Committee requesting placement of a historic building on the City's Historic Register, so the owner is eligible for historic preservation incentives. The owner commits to recording the City's Historic Preservation Agreement on title before obtaining benefits. Ordinance: LBMC Chapter 25.45. The form carries no tailored submittal checklist.

application_index.title: Wireless Facility Permit Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: "A WFP is required for any new, collocated, or modified wireless facility located within the public right-of-way, and may take the form of a Planning Commission Wireless Facility Permit or an Administrative Wireless Facility Permit (Director approval)." Terms are defined in LBMC Chapter 11.06. This form predates the July 2026 revision; it is stamped "Updated April 2026".

application_index.title: Artist Occupancy Permit Application
application_index.detail: the City requires certification as a working artist to qualify for an Artist Work/Live space in the M-1A and M-1B, C-N, LBP, downtown specific plan, R-2, and R-3 districts. The application is submitted to the Cultural Arts Department and turns on a body of work, formal arts training, exhibition history, and letters of recommendation. The applicant files it directly with the City.

application_index.title: Short-Term Lodging — Administrative Use Permit Application
application_index.detail: the City's link to this form serves an account login page rather than the PDF, and its Applications & Handouts page carries only the link title, so no trigger text of the City's own is available to state here. The applicant files it directly with the City.

application_index.title: Temporary Use Permit Application
application_index.detail: trigger as the City states it: temporary uses are governed by LBMC Chapter 25.05.035 "and may be permitted when such activities are desirable for the community and are consistent with the health, safety and general welfare of persons residing and working in the community." The City states temporary uses of five days or less may be processed administratively and those longer than five days go to the Planning Commission. The applicant files it directly with the City.
